gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a sump pump draws 0 W between float cycles. A station's ECO or no-load AC shut-off can therefore kill the outlet before the pit refills. BLUETTI's AC300 manual says ECO turns AC off below 30 W over 4 h, and The Technology Man reports the Elite 300's Eco mode turns AC off with no load. If ECO is switched off to prevent that, the inverter's own idle draw (about 19 W, measured on an Elite 300) uses about 226 Wh over 12 hours, and no runtime table counts it.
standout_why: I compared four pages. RunTimeFit (cited, the source of ChatGPT's PECRON pick) says 'Most makers don't publish inverter idle draw, so the hours leave it out' and never mentions ECO or no-load auto-off. Tested Watts (cited) gives the Zoeller M53's 25.9 A start and 10–20 ms UPS switchover, but says nothing about auto-off or idle draw. OutageReadyHQ (cited) gives running and starting watts by HP only. The Home Battery Report (cited) covers LRA (F3800 Plus 80 A), surge duration (DELTA Pro Ultra 10.8 kW for 10 s) and 240 V. None of them says the AC outlet can switch itself off while the pump is idle, or counts 12 hours of inverter idle draw. Our current page also lacks both.
decides: This doesn't change which station is biggest, but it adds a condition the plan depends on: ECO or AC auto-off must be disabled, or the pump has no power when the float closes. Once ECO is off, idle draw comes out of the budget. For the Elite 300 our 25 %-duty row drops from 11.9 h to about 10.9 h (2,380 Wh usable ÷ (200 W average pump + 19 W idle), using our page's own 800 W × 25 % basis). That pushes it under 12 h, so the 12-hour pick should be the 3.4 kWh-plus ALLPOWERS R4000 or larger (F3800 Plus, S5000). The page needs a 'turn off ECO / set AC timeout to Never' step.

findings.label: Eco mode turns AC off when nothing is drawing power
findings.value: AC subsystem turns off with no load in Eco mode; with Eco off, it stayed on for 16 h with no load
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 300 Review – 3kWh Capacity – But There Are Compromises (The Technology Man, Gidon, 2026-03-25)
findings.note: Quote: 'In Eco mode, the AC subsystem will turn off if there's no load attached, but with Eco mode turned off I left the unit overnight for 16 hours with no load connected.' The review doesn't give the Elite 300's ECO threshold or factory default.

findings.label: AC idle (self) draw with no load, measured
findings.value: about 19 W (100 % to 90 % over 16 h, AC on, no load)
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 300 Review – 3kWh Capacity – But There Are Compromises (The Technology Man, Gidon, 2026-03-25)
findings.note: Reviewer: 'just having AC turned on uses around 19 W per hour'. Check: 10 % × 3,014.4 Wh = 301 Wh ÷ 16 h = 18.8 W. Over a 12 h outage that is about 226 Wh, or 7.5 % of capacity. The reviewer's '20 A = 4,600 W' implies a 230 V unit, so the US 120 V idle draw may differ.

findings.label: Motor start test (inrush), measured
findings.value: started a load pulling over 20 A (over 4,600 W) at startup; a load pulling over 26 A (over 6,000 W) at startup was too much
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 300 Review – 3kWh Capacity – But There Are Compromises (The Technology Man, Gidon, 2026-03-25)
findings.note: Clamp-meter readings by the reviewer, apparently at 230 V (the review's own watt figures imply it). Tested Watts gives the Zoeller M53 1/3-class pump about 3,000 W at start, which is under the load that started.

findings.label: Power Lifting is not a motor start allowance
findings.value: 4,800 W Power Lifting: disabled by default, pure resistive loads only, real output stays 2,400 W
findings.note: Quotes: 'The mode is disabled by default and is intended only for pure resistive loads'; 'It is also not a startup allowance for motors or compressors.' StorageReview measured an 8 ms switchover to battery.

findings.label: ECO AC auto-off rule in BLUETTI's own manual
findings.value: AC output off if AC load is under 30 W over 4 hours
findings.note: Quote: 'ECO: The power saving mode of the unit to turn off the AC output to conserve energy if the AC load is less than 30W over 4 hours.' This is the AC300, not the Elite 300. A sump pump sitting idle between cycles in a slow-filling pit draws 0 W, so this rule would cut its power.
